text:
liam: heads up — perf CI flagged a regression after merge to main, seen as higher p95 token latency on long-context workloads (~4k).
ci-perf-bot: automated perf check failed on job runtime/perf/long_context (build: f7a3b9). p95 increased 2.5x, throughput -40%. See artifacts: https://ci.internal/redwood/f7a3b9/artifacts
anya: that was my change to kernel selection heuristics (PR #7891). i adjusted the candidate scoring to favor fewer CUDA kernels but with larger launch sizes. expected wins on short sequences, worried about tail with kv-heavy runs.
miguel: can we bisect quickly? if it's that PR we should either revert or hotfix. this is blocking the release.
liam: doing quick git-bisect now on a copy of the perf runner, will report.
liam: bisect points to f1d2c3 (merge of #7891) as first bad commit. stack traces point at kernel_selector.cpp:selectBestPlan() and at the new heuristic path.
sophie: suggested mitigations: 1) revert the merge on main immediately. 2) open a hotfix branch from the last known-good tag (v1.12.3) and cherry-pick a minimal patch that keeps old behavior for long contexts.
anya: i can push a follow-up patch that adds a gate based on seq_len distribution. patch local perf shows regression gone.
ryan: i'll prepare the backport PR and run the perf suite against the hotfix branch. can someone outline exact git steps we want?
sophie: run these:
```
# create hotfix branch from v1.12.3
git checkout -b hotfix/v1.12.4 v1.12.3
# cherry-pick the revert commit or apply patch
git cherry-pick -x <commit-of-fix>
# push and open PR against release/v1.12
git push origin hotfix/v1.12.4
```
liam: instead of a full revert we prefer a targeted patch (adds seq_len threshold). cherry-pick hash: a9b7e2 (local).
anya: pushed PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/7904 — patch adds short_seq heuristic only when avg_seq_len < 512, defaults preserved. includes unit tests and perf job config.
ci-perf-bot: perf run queued for PR 7904 (runner: long_context).
ryan: running local perf with the same dataset used by CI, baseline main f7a3b9 vs hotfix a9b7e2: p95 1.2s -> 0.48s for 4k context. throughput back to expected. numbers attached.
miguel: thanks. next steps: merge hotfix to release branch, backport to main? we should put a strict rollout policy for the next main merge.
sophie: merging to release/v1.12 now, will create a backport PR to main which restores a safer default and leaves the heuristic behind feature-flag.
liam: creating a release candidate: v1.12.4-rc1, tagging a9b7e2.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: 2 instances in us-west-2 with tag v1.12.4-rc1. monitor window 30m.
ci-perf-bot: final perf run on release branch passed. p95 and throughput in expected range.
ryan: verified canary traces: kv cache hit behavior normal, batching aligns to expected bins, kernel selection path now falls back to old plan for seq_len > 1024.
anya: sorry for the break, added extra logging and a small opt-in flag so we can experiment safely. will follow up with docs.
miguel: add a postmortem note: root cause = overaggressive heuristic that optimized for launch latency but increased kernel swaps and KV cache thrashing at high sequence lengths.
liam: agreed — i'll open a short postmortem thread in #postmortems and link PRs + perf artifacts. closing the rollout blocker once rc merges to main and canary finishes. :thumbsup:
sophie: merged to release/v1.12 and opened backport PR to main: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/7909
liam: last check: canary healthy, merging RC into main now.
deploy-bot: release main@a9b7e2 deployed to prod with immediate fallback policy active.
ci-perf-bot: nightly regression suite ran — green.
liam: thanks everyone — great rapid response. we'll follow up with a short blameless postmortem and schedule a deeper perf test for kernel selection matrix.
anya: will add a follow-up test matrix.
ryan: verified metrics dashboard shows 0 regressions after rollout.
miguel: closing thread, will update the release notes and changelog. :white_check_mark:
